crossref.title: Data from Germline Pathogenic <i>DROSHA</i> Variants Are Linked to Pineoblastoma and Wilms Tumor Predisposition
crossref.abstract: <jats:p><div>AbstractPurpose:<p><i>DROSHA</i>, <i>DGCR8</i>, and <i>DICER1</i> regulate miRNA biogenesis and are commonly mutated in cancer. Although <i>DGCR8</i> and <i>DICER1</i> germline pathogenic variants (GPV) cause autosomal dominant tumor predisposition, no association between <i>DROSHA</i> GPVs and clinical phenotypes has been reported.</p>Experimental Design:<p>After obtaining informed consent, sequencing was performed on germline and tumor samples from all patients. The occurrence of germline <i>DROSHA</i> GPVs was investigated in large pediatric and adult cancer datasets. The population prevalence of <i>DROSHA</i> GPVs was investigated in the UK Biobank and Geisinger DiscovEHR cohorts.</p>Results:<p>We describe nine children from eight families with heterozygous <i>DROSHA</i> GPVs and a diagnosis of pineoblastoma (<i>n</i> = 8) or Wilms tumor (<i>n</i> = 1). A somatic second hit in <i>DROSHA</i> was detected in all eight tumors analyzed. All pineoblastoma tumors analyzed were classified as miRNA processing–altered 1 subtype. We estimate the population prevalence of germline <i>DROSHA</i> loss-of-function variants to be 1:3,875 to 1:4,843 but find no evidence for increased adult cancer risk.</p>Conclusions:<p>This is the first report of <i>DROSHA-</i>related tumor predisposition. As pineoblastoma and Wilms tumor are also associated with <i>DICER1</i> GPVs, our results suggest that the tissues of origin for these tumors are uniquely tolerant of general miRNA loss. The miRNA processing–altered 1 pineoblastoma subtype is associated with older age of diagnosis and better outcomes than other subtypes, suggesting <i>DROSHA</i> GPV status may have important clinical and prognostic significance. We suggest that genetic testing for <i>DROSHA</i> GPVs be considered for patients with pineoblastoma, Wilms tumor, or other <i>DICER1</i>-/<i>DGCR8</i>-related conditions and propose surveillance recommendations through research studies for individuals with <i>DROSHA</i> GPVs.</p></div></jats:p>
